company.name: Simmer
company.description: A recipe and meal-planning app with a free tier and a paid plan. Most new users come from organic search and paid social.

title: Simmer: where did the signups go?
brief: New signups fell 17% in the last 7 days compared with the week before. Engineering shipped a new app version the same week, and the CEO is convinced it broke signup. Work out what actually happened before anyone starts a rollback.

rootCause.summary: The paid social campaign ended and nothing replaced it, so paid social signups fell by about 85%.
rootCause.explanation: The drop is entirely in the paid social channel, on every platform and in every country, including the web, which did not get a release. The 6.4.0 release is a coincidence of timing.
rootCause.idealAction: Do not roll back 6.4.0. Agree with marketing whether to restart or replace the paid social budget, and reset the signup target to the organic baseline.
idealPath: Break down by channel: paid social collapses, other channels are flat
Check the web: it fell too, so the mobile release is not the cause
Check India: the holiday dip is small and short

falseLeads.explanation: 6.4.0 shipped the same day, which makes it a tempting suspect, but users on 6.4.0 sign up at the same rate as on 6.3.1, and the web, which has no release, dropped as well.
The holiday in India lowers signups there for two days, a small, short dip that recovers on its own.
